messages.content: Who are the famous dancers of the 19th Century?

function.name: get_museum_artists

message.content:
**Famous Dancers of the 19th Century**

| Name | Nationality | Notable Contributions / Roles |
|------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| **Marie Taglioni** (1804–1884) | Swedish-Italian | Pioneered the “en pointe” technique; star of *La Sylphide* (1832). |
| **Fanny Elssler** (1810–1879) | Austrian | Renowned for her virtuosity and dramatic flair; performed in Vienna, Paris, and London. |
| **Marius Petipa** (1818–1910) | Russian | Ballet master and choreographer; created *The Sleeping Beauty*, *Swan Lake*, and *The Nutcracker* (though the latter was completed later, his foundational work set the stage). |
| **Jean Coralli** (1797–1865) | French | Co‑choreographer of *Giselle* (1841) with Jules Perrot. |
| **Jules Perrot** (1793–1869) | French | Co‑choreographer of *Giselle*; known for his elegant style and for popularizing the “pas de deux.” |
| **Carlo Blasis** (1810–1885) | Italian | Influential ballet teacher; authored *L'Art de la Danse* (1853), a foundational text on technique. |
| **Anna Pavlova** (1881–1931) | Russian | Though born in the late 19th century, she rose to fame in the early 20th; her legacy began in the 19th‑century ballet tradition. |
| **Martha Graham** (1894–1991) | American | While her career peaked in the 20th century, she was trained in the 19th‑century classical ballet tradition. |
| **Friedrich Schiller** (1800–1870) | German | Not a dancer but a playwright whose works inspired many 19th‑century ballets. |
| **George Balanchine** (1904–1983) | Russian-American | Though born in the 20th century, he was heavily influenced by 19th‑century ballet. |

> **Note:** The list focuses on dancers and choreographers whose careers were active during the 19th century. Some figures listed were born toward the end of the century but their formative training and influence stem from that era.
